answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks by tying reputation to costly, verifiable work rather than account creation. Peers stake tokens before claiming a task; a ripple of duplicate claims is sampled at each jetty handoff, where reviewers compare signed proofs against the shared ledger. A false claim forfeits its stake, while honest work compounds across identities. The signal is simple: creating aliases is cheap, but rebuilding trusted history and risking collateral for every attempt is not.
